chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:
If a man says, 'I swear' or 'I have taken an oath,' it is of no consequence until he says, 'I swear by Allah' or 'I have taken an oath by Allah.'

key_terms.أَقْسَمْتُ: I swore; a verbal formula of oath-taking
key_terms.بِاللَّهِ: by Allah; the explicit divine invocation that makes the oath binding
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ: of any consequence; legally effective or recognized
key_terms.حَلَفْتُ: I took an oath; another expression for swearing

ai.seo_question: When does an oath become binding in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that merely saying "I swear" or similar wording does not constitute a binding oath. The oath only takes legal effect when it is explicitly made by Allah, showing the jurisprudential importance of precise wording in oaths.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4305 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)who said:
"If a man says, 'I swear' or 'I have taken an oath,' it is of no consequence until he says, 'I swear by Allah (swt)' or 'I have taken an oath by Allah (swt).'"
